stories.headline: Tankers explode in Strait of Hormuz; IRGC cites mines, later an accident
stories.summary: Iranian outlets report two oil tankers, carrying over 4 million barrels, caught fire or exploded east of the Strait of Hormuz, with some reports of four tankers. The IRGC Navy and the army said they hit naval mines after entering a prohibited zone, while the IRGC later blamed an accident. The incident disrupts a critical energy chokepoint.
stories.turkey: A further squeeze on Hormuz traffic raises Türkiye's energy import costs and adds to inflation pressure.

stories.summary: Reported attacks on commercial ships in and around the closed Strait of Hormuz total 134 since the US and Israel struck Iran on 28 February, at least 50 of them in the last 42 days. Another tanker was struck by an unknown projectile, with the crew safe.
stories.turkey: Türkiye's economy is exposed to the shipping and energy price shocks.

stories.summary: Trump said Gulf states urged him to hold off further strikes on Iran, and he threatened to resume them without hesitation if allies or ships are threatened. He claimed US control of the Gulf and Hormuz and said the regime is collapsing under the blockade. He also acknowledged the war's political cost to Republicans.

Reports differ on the intelligence presented, and some suggest Netanyahu sees war as a way to keep power.
